verses.text: 1:1King David was old and advanced in days; and they wrapped him in garments, but he did not grow warm.
1:2His attendants said, “Let them seek a young virgin for our lord the king. She shall attend the king and keep him warm; she shall lie with him, and our lord the king will become warm.”
1:3And they sought a fair young woman throughout all the territory of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
1:4The young woman was very fair; she kept the king warm and served him, but the king did not know her.
1:5Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, “I will reign!” He prepared chariots and horsemen for himself, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
1:6His father had never restrained him by saying, “Why have you done this?” He too was very handsome in appearance, and his mother bore him after Absalom.
1:7He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest, and they helped by following Adonijah.
1:8But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men were not following Adonijah.
1:9Adonijah sacrificed sheep, calves, and lambs beside the stone of Zoheleth, near the spring of Rogel. He invited all his brothers and all the prominent men of Judah, the king’s attendants.
1:10But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.
1:11Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while our lord David does not know it?
1:12Now come, let me give you counsel, and rescue your life and the life of your son Solomon.

1:13Come, enter King David’s presence and say to him, ‘Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying, “Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne”? Why, then, has Adonijah become king?’
1:14Behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and complete your words.”
1:15Bathsheba entered the king’s chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was ministering to the king.
1:16Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. The king said, “What is your concern?”
1:17She said, “My lord the king, you swore by the Lord your God to your servant, saying, ‘Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’
1:18Now behold, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
1:19He has sacrificed calves, lambs, and sheep in abundance. He has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the force, but he has not invited your servant Solomon.
1:20As for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are directed toward you, for you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
1:21When my lord the king lies down with his fathers, my son Solomon and I will be sinners.”
1:22While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
1:23The king was told, “Behold, Nathan the prophet!” He came before the king and prostrated himself before the king, face to the ground.
1:24Nathan said, “My lord the king, you said, ‘Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’

1:25For he went down this day and sacrificed calves, lambs, and sheep in abundance. He invited all the king’s sons, the commanders of the force, and Abiathar the priest. Behold, they are eating and drinking before him and have said, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
1:26But me—me, your servant—and Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon, he did not invite.
1:27Has this matter come about through my lord the king without your informing your servant who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?”
1:28David answered, “Call Bathsheba to me.” She came before the king and stood before him.
1:29The king swore, saying, “As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every affliction,
1:30just as I swore to you by the Lord, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,’ so I will indeed do this very day.”
1:31Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king. She said, “May my lord King David live for ever!”
1:32King David said, “Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada to me.” They came before the king.
1:33The king said to them, “Take your lord’s servants with you. Mount my son Solomon on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
1:34There let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. Sound the horn and say, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
1:35He shall sit on my throne and reign in my place; I have commanded that he be leader over Israel and Judah.”
1:36Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, “So be it! May the Lord, the God of my lord the king, confirm it so.
1:37As the Lord has been with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”
1:38Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down. They seated Solomon on King David’s mule and led him away to Gihon.
1:39Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. He sounded the horn, and all the people said, “Long live King Solomon!”
1:40All the people went up after him. They danced in choruses and rejoiced with great joy, and the earth burst at their sound.
1:41Adonijah and all his guests heard it, and they finished eating. Joab heard the sound of the horn and said, “What is this sound of the echoing city?”
1:42While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, “Come in, for you are a man of ability; bring good news!”
1:43Jonathan answered, “Indeed, our lord King David has made Solomon king!
1:44The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites. They seated him on the king’s mule.
1:45Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They came up from there rejoicing, and the city echoed. That is the sound you heard.
1:46Solomon has sat on the royal throne.

1:47The king’s servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, ‘May God make the name of your son Solomon better than your name and make his throne greater than your throne.’ The king prostrated himself on his bed.
1:48The king also said this: ‘Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who this day has given one from my offspring to sit on my throne while my eyes see it!’”
1:49All Adonijah’s guests were astonished and rose. Each went his own way.
1:50Adonijah was afraid of Solomon. He rose, went away, and took hold of the horns of the altar.

1:51Solomon was told, “Behold, Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. He is holding fast to the altar’s horns, saying, ‘Let King Solomon swear to me this day whether he will not put his servant to death with the sword.’”
1:52Solomon said, “If he becomes a man of ability, not one of his hairs shall fall to the ground! But if wickedness is found in him, he shall be put to death.”
1:53King Solomon sent and brought him down from the altar. He came and prostrated himself before King Solomon. Solomon said to him, “Come now, go to your house.”
2:1When David’s days drew near for him to die, he commanded his son Solomon, saying,
2:2“I myself am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and be a man,

2:3and keep the charge of the Lord your God: walk in His ways, keeping His commandments, statutes, and judgments written in Moses’ law, so that you may understand what you will do in everything that I command you,

2:4so that the Lord may establish His word which He spoke, saying, ‘If your sons guard their way, walking before Me in truth with all their heart and all their soul,’ saying, ‘A man shall not be cut off for you from Israel’s throne.’

2:5You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s forces, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, setting the blood of war in peace, and put innocent blood on the belt around his waist and the sandal on his foot.
2:6Act according to your wisdom, and do not bring his gray hair down to Hades in peace.
2:7Show mercy to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they came near to me in this way when I fled from your brother Absalom.

2:8Behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera, a son of the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a painful curse on the day I went to Camps. He came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, ‘I will not put you to death with the sword.’
2:9You must certainly not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You will know what to do to him, and you shall bring his gray hair down to Hades with blood.”
2:10David lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
2:11David’s reign over Israel lasted forty years. He reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
2:12Solomon sat on the throne of his father David when he was twelve years old, and his kingdom was firmly prepared.
2:13Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, and prostrated himself before her. She said, “Is your coming peaceful?” He said, “Peaceful.
2:14I have a word for you.” She said to him, “Speak.”
2:15He said to her, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel set its face toward me to reign. But the kingdom turned and became my brother’s, for it became his from the Lord.
2:16Now I have one request to ask of you; do not turn away your face.” Bathsheba said to him, “Speak.”
2:17He said to her, “Please speak to King Solomon—for he will not turn his face away from you—and he will give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.”
2:18Bathsheba said, “Very well. I will speak to the king about you.”

2:19Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him about Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and kissed her, then sat on his throne. A throne was placed for the king’s mother, and she sat at his right.
2:20She said to him, “I have one small request to ask of you; do not turn away your face.” The king said to her, “Ask, my mother, for I will not turn you away.”
2:21She said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as a wife.”

2:22King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you ask for Abishag for Adonijah? Ask for the kingdom for him too, for he is my elder brother! Abiathar the priest is his, and Joab son of Zeruiah, the commander-in-chief, is his companion!”
2:23King Solomon swore by the Lord, “May God do thus to me and add more, for Adonijah has spoken this word against his own life!
2:24Now, as the Lord lives, who prepared me and placed me on the throne of my father David—He made a house for me, as the Lord spoke—Adonijah shall be put to death this day.”
2:25King Solomon sent through Benaiah son of Jehoiada and had Adonijah killed. Adonijah died that day.

2:26The king said to Abiathar the priest, “Go quickly to Anathoth, to your field. You are a man deserving death this day, but I will not put you to death, because you did carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant before my father and did suffer all the hardships my father suffered.”
2:27Solomon expelled Abiathar from being priest to the Lord, fulfilling the Lord’s word which He had spoken concerning Eli’s house at Shiloh.
2:28The report reached Joab son of Zeruiah, for Joab had followed Adonijah but had not followed Solomon. Joab fled to the Lord’s dwelling and held fast to the horns of the altar.

2:29Solomon was told, “Joab has fled to the Lord’s tent and is holding fast to the altar’s horns.” Solomon sent to Joab, asking, “What has happened to you, that you have fled to the altar?” Joab said, “I was afraid of you, and I fled to the Lord.” King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, kill him and bury him.”

2:30Benaiah son of Jehoiada came to Joab in the Lord’s tent and said to him, “Thus says the king: Come out.” Joab said, “I am not coming out, for I will die here.” Benaiah son of Jehoiada returned and said to the king, “This is what Joab has said, and this is how he has answered me.”
2:31The king said to him, “Go and do to him as he has said. Kill him and bury him, and this day remove from me and my father’s house the blood Joab shed without cause.

2:32The Lord returned the blood of his injustice upon his own head, because he struck two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword, while my father David did not know of their blood: Abner son of Ner, commander-in-chief of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander-in-chief of Judah.
2:33Their blood was returned upon his head and the head of his offspring for ever. But for David, his offspring, his house, and his throne may there be peace from the Lord for ever.”
2:34Benaiah son of Jehoiada came upon Joab, put him to death, and buried him at his house in the wilderness.

2:35The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in the military command in Joab’s place. The kingdom was being established in Jerusalem, and the king appointed Zadok the priest as first priest in Abiathar’s place.
2:35aThe Lord gave Solomon discernment, exceedingly great wisdom, and breadth of heart like the sand beside the sea.
2:35bSolomon’s discernment greatly surpassed the discernment of all the sons of old and all the discerning men of Egypt.

2:35cHe took Pharaoh’s daughter and brought her into the City of David until he had first finished his own house, the Lord’s house, and Jerusalem’s surrounding wall. He built and completed them in seven years.
2:35dSolomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country.
2:35eSolomon made the sea, the supports, the great washbasins, the pillars, the courtyard’s fountain, and the bronze sea.

2:35fHe built the citadel and its battlements and cut through the City of David. Thus Pharaoh’s daughter would go up from the City of David to her house, which he built for her. Then he built the citadel.
2:35gSolomon offered three whole burnt offerings and peace offerings in the year on the altar he built for the Lord, and burned incense before the Lord. He completed the house.
2:35hThese were the officials appointed over Solomon’s works: three thousand six hundred overseers of the people doing the works.
2:35iHe built Assour, Megiddo, Gezer, Upper Beth-horon, and Baalath.
2:35kOnly after he had built the Lord’s house and Jerusalem’s surrounding wall—after these things—did he build these cities.
2:35lWhile David was still alive, he commanded Solomon: “Behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera, a descendant of the Benjaminite, from Hebron.
2:35mHe cursed me with a painful curse on the day I was going to Camps.
2:35nHe was coming down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, ‘He shall not be put to death with the sword.’
2:35oNow do not hold him guiltless, for you are a discerning man. You will know what to do to him, and you shall bring his gray hair down to Hades with blood.”
2:36The king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and stay there. You shall not go out from there anywhere.
2:37On the day you go out and cross the Wadi Kidron, know for certain that you shall surely die. Your blood shall be upon your own head.” The king made him swear that day.
2:38Shimei said to the king, “The word you have spoken is good, my lord the king. Your servant will do so.” Shimei stayed in Jerusalem three years.
2:39After three years, two of Shimei’s slaves fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, “Behold, your slaves are in Gath.”
2:40Shimei rose, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to seek out his slaves. Shimei went and brought his slaves back from Gath.
2:41Solomon was told, “Shimei went from Jerusalem to Gath and brought back his slaves.”

2:42The king sent for Shimei and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the Lord and solemnly warn you, ‘On the day you leave Jerusalem and go to the right or left, know for certain that you shall surely die’?
2:43Why have you not kept the Lord’s oath and the command I laid upon you?”
2:44The king said to Shimei, “You know all your wickedness which your heart knew, the things you did to my father David. The Lord has repaid your wickedness upon your head.
2:45But King Solomon is blessed, and David’s throne shall be prepared before the Lord for ever.”
2:46King Solomon commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He went out and killed Shimei, and Shimei died.
2:46aKing Solomon was exceedingly discerning and wise. Judah and Israel were exceedingly numerous, like the sand beside the sea in multitude, eating, drinking, and rejoicing.
2:46bSolomon ruled among all the kingdoms. They brought gifts and served Solomon all the days of his life.
2:46cSolomon began to open up the resources of Lebanon,
2:46dand he built Thermai in the wilderness.

2:46eThis was Solomon’s midday meal: thirty kors of fine flour, sixty kors of pounded meal, ten choice calves, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, and choice pasture-fed birds.
2:46fFor he ruled throughout the region beyond the River, from Raphi to Gaza, among all the kings beyond the River.
2:46gHe had peace on every side around him. Judah and Israel lived securely, each beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, eating and drinking, from Dan to Beersheba, all Solomon’s days.

2:46hThese were Solomon’s officials: Azariah son of Zadok the priest; Ornia son of Nathan, chief of the supervisors; Edram over his house; Souba the scribe; Basa son of Achithalam, the recorder; Abi son of Joab, commander-in-chief; Achire son of Edrai over the burdens; Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the court administration and the brickworks; and Zachour son of Nathan, the counselor.
2:46iSolomon had forty thousand broodmares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.
2:46kHe ruled among all the kings from the River to the land of foreigners and to Egypt’s borders.
2:46lSolomon son of David reigned over Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.
3:2The people, however, were burning incense at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the Lord’s name.
3:3Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the ordinances of his father David; however, he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
3:4He rose and went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the highest place and a great one. Solomon offered a thousand whole burnt offerings on the altar at Gibeon.
3:5The Lord appeared to Solomon in sleep at night. The Lord said to Solomon, “Ask a request for yourself.”

3:6Solomon said, “Thou showedst great mercy to Thy servant David my father, as he walked before Thee in truth, righteousness, and uprightness of heart with Thee. Thou keptest this great mercy for him, placing his son on his throne, as it is this day.
3:7Now, Lord my God, Thou hast placed Thy servant in place of my father David. I am a little child and do not know my going out or my coming in.
3:8Thy servant is among Thy people whom Thou didst choose, a numerous people who cannot be numbered.
3:9Give Thy servant a heart to hear and to judge Thy people in righteousness, discerning between good and evil; for who can judge this weighty people of Thine?”
3:10It pleased the Lord that Solomon had asked this.
3:11The Lord said to him, “Because you have asked this of Me and have not asked for many days for yourself, or wealth, or the lives of your enemies, but have asked for understanding to hear judgment,
3:12behold, I have done according to your word. Behold, I have given you a discerning and wise heart, so that no one like you has been before you, and no one like you shall arise after you.
3:13I have also given you what you did not ask: both wealth and glory, so that no man like you has been among the kings.
3:14If you walk in My way, keeping My commandments and ordinances as your father David walked, I will multiply your days.”

3:15Solomon awoke: it was a dream. He rose and came to Jerusalem, and stood before the altar that was before the ark of the Lord’s covenant in Zion. He offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a great feast for himself and all his attendants.
3:16Then two women who were prostitutes appeared before the king and stood before him.
3:17One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in one house, and we gave birth in the house.
3:18On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together, with no one in the house except the two of us.
3:19This woman’s son died during the night when she lay on him.
3:20She rose in the middle of the night and took my son from my arms. She laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead son in my bosom.
3:21I rose in the morning to nurse my son, and that child was dead. I looked carefully at him in the morning, and he was not my son whom I had borne.”
3:22The other woman said, “No! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.” Thus they spoke before the king.
3:23The king said to them, “You say, ‘This is my son, the living one, and her son is the dead one.’ And you say, ‘No! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.’”
3:24The king said, “Bring me a sword.” They brought the sword before the king.
3:25The king said, “Divide the living nursing child in two. Give half of it to this woman and half of it to this woman.”

3:26The woman whose son was alive answered the king, for her womb was stirred for her son. She said, “Please, my lord, give her the child! You must not put him to death!” But the other said, “He shall belong to neither me nor her. Divide him.”
3:27The king answered, “Give the child to the woman who said, ‘Give it to her,’ and you must not put him to death. She is his mother.”
3:28All Israel heard this judgment the king had given, and they feared the king, for they saw that God’s discernment was within him to carry out justice.
4:1King Solomon reigned over Israel.
4:2These were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok;
4:3Elihoreph and Ahijah son of Saba were scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
4:4Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
4:5Ornia son of Nathan was over the appointed officers; Zabud son of Nathan was the king’s companion;
4:6Achiel was household steward; Eliab son of Saph was over the clan; Adoniram son of Ephra was over the tributes.
4:7Solomon had twelve appointed officers over all Israel to provide for the king and his household. Each was responsible for providing one month in the year.
4:8These were their names: Benor, in Ephraim’s hill country—one;
4:9the son of Rechab, in Machemas, Bethalamin, Beth-shemesh, and Ailon as far as Beth-hanan—one;
4:10the son of Esoth, in Berbethnema, Lousamencha, and Rhesphara;
4:11Chinanadab and Anaphathi, husband of Tableth; a daughter of Solomon was his wife—one;
4:12Baccha son of Ahilud, over Taanach, Megiddo, and all the house of San beside Sesathan below Esrae, and from Baisaphoud, Abel-meholah, as far as Maeber Loukam—one;
4:13the son of Geber, in Remath-gilead; Eregaba’s district in Bashan belonged to his charge, sixty great walled cities with bronze bars—one;
4:14Ahinadab son of Achel, in Mahanaim—one;
4:15Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he too took Solomon’s daughter Basemath as a wife—one;
4:16Baana son of Hushai, in Maalath—one;
4:17Shammah son of Elah, in Benjamin;
4:18Geber son of Adai, in Gad’s land, the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan; and one officer in Judah’s land;
4:19Jehoshaphat son of Phouasoud, in Issachar.

5:1The appointed officers thus provided for King Solomon and all the orders for the king’s table, each in his month; they did not depart from an instruction. They brought barley and straw for the horses and chariots to the place where the king would be, each according to his assignment.
5:2These were Solomon’s requirements for one day: thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of pounded meal,
5:3ten choice calves, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, and choice birds—fattened provisions.
5:4For he was ruler beyond the River, and he had peace on every side around him.
5:9The Lord gave Solomon discernment, very great wisdom, and abundance of heart like the sand beside the sea.
5:10Solomon increased greatly beyond the discernment of all ancient people and beyond all the discerning people of Egypt.
5:11He became wiser than all people; he became wiser than Gaithan the Ezraite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mal.
5:12Solomon spoke three thousand parables, and his songs numbered five thousand.
5:13He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing through the wall. He spoke about livestock, birds, creeping things, and fish.
5:14All the peoples came to hear Solomon’s wisdom, and he received gifts from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
5:14aSolomon took Pharaoh’s daughter as his wife and brought her into the City of David until he finished the Lord’s house, his own house, and Jerusalem’s wall.

5:14bThen Pharaoh king of Egypt went up, captured Gezer beforehand, and burned it and the Canaanite who lived in Mergab. Pharaoh gave them as parting gifts to his daughter, Solomon’s wife; and Solomon built Gezer.
5:15Hiram king of Tyre sent his attendants to anoint Solomon in place of David his father, for Hiram had always loved David.
5:16Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,
5:17“You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the Lord put them beneath the footsteps of his feet.
5:18But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side; there is no plotter and no evil encounter.

5:19Behold, I intend to build a house for the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord God told my father David: ‘Your son, whom I shall place on your throne in your place, shall build the house for My name.’

5:20Now command that they cut timber from Lebanon for me. Behold, my servants are with your servants, and I will pay you the wages of your service according to whatever you say; for you know that no one among us knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”
5:21When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be God this day, who has given David a discerning son over this great people!”
5:22He sent to Solomon, saying, “I have heard about everything you did send to me. I will fulfill all your wishes: cedar and pine timber.

5:23My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea. I will make them into rafts as far as the place you send me word about, and shake them apart there; you shall take them away. You shall fulfill my wish by providing loaves for my household.”
5:24Hiram supplied Solomon with cedars and all that he desired.
5:25Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat and machir for his household, and twenty thousand beth of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram each year.
5:26The Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a covenant between themselves.
5:27The king raised a levy from all Israel; the levy was thirty thousand men.
5:28He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in shifts: one month they were in Lebanon and two months at their home. Adoniram was over the levy.
5:29Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
5:30besides the chiefs appointed over Solomon’s works, three thousand six hundred overseers who performed the works.
5:32They prepared the stones and timber for three years.
6:1In the four hundred fortieth year of the exodus of the sons of Israel from Egypt, in the fourth year, in the second month, when King Solomon reigned over Israel,
6:1athe king commanded, and they carried great, costly stones for the house’s foundation, and unhewn stones.
6:1bSolomon’s sons and Hiram’s sons hewed them and laid them down.
6:1cIn the fourth year he laid the foundation of the Lord’s house in the month of Niso, the second month.
6:1dIn the eleventh year, in the month of Baal, which is the eighth month, the house was completed in every detail and according to its entire arrangement.
6:2The house that King Solomon built for the Lord was forty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty-five cubits high.
6:3The porch in front of the temple was twenty cubits long across the house’s width, and ten cubits wide in front of the house. He built the house and completed it.
6:4He made recessed, concealed windows for the house.
6:5He placed beams all around against the house’s wall, for the temple and the inner sanctuary; he made side chambers all around.

6:6The lowest side chamber was five cubits wide, the middle six, and the third seven cubits wide; for he left a space all around the house, outside the house, so that they would not take hold of the house’s walls.
6:7While the house was being built, it was built of sharply cut, unworked stones. No hammer, axe, or any iron implement was heard in the house while it was being built.
6:8The entrance of the lowest side chamber was beneath the house’s right shoulder. A winding ascent led to the middle tier, and from the middle to the third story.
6:9He built the house and completed it, and furnished the house with a coffered cedar ceiling.
6:10He built the connecting structures throughout the whole house, five cubits high, and held the connecting structure together with cedar timbers.

6:15He built the house’s walls with cedar timbers, from the floor of the house up to the beams and up to the walls. He fitted the interior continuously with wooden panels and covered the inside of the house with pine boards.
6:16He built the twenty cubits at the end of the house, the one side from the floor to the beams, and made the inner sanctuary into the Holy of Holies.
6:17The temple was forty cubits long in front
6:19of the inner sanctuary, inside the house, to place the ark of the Lord’s covenant there.
6:20It was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He covered it with refined gold, and he made an altar
6:21in front of the inner sanctuary, and he covered it with gold.
6:22He covered the whole house with gold until the entire house was finished.
6:23In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, their measured size ten cubits.
6:24One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and its other wing was five cubits: ten cubits from one wingtip to the other.
6:25So it was with the second cherub; both had one measure and one finished form.
6:26The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was that of the second cherub.

6:27Both cherubim were within the innermost house. He spread their wings: one wing touched one wall, and a wing touched the other wall; their wings toward the middle of the house touched wing to wing.
6:28He covered the cherubim with gold.
6:29On all the house’s walls around he engraved cherubim with a carving tool; palm trees were in the inner and outer rooms.
6:30He covered the floor of the house with gold, in the innermost and outermost rooms.
6:31For the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made juniper-wood doors and fivefold doorposts,
6:32and two pine-wood doors with carvings engraved on them: cherubim, palm trees, and spreading petals. He covered them with gold, and the gold came down over the cherubim and palm trees.
6:33Likewise he made the temple entrance: juniper-wood doorposts, porticoes fourfold,
6:34and both doors were of pine wood: one door had two leaves and their pivots, and the other door had two leaves that turned.
6:35There were engraved cherubim, palm trees, and spreading petals, covered with gold brought down over the relief.
6:36He built the innermost court with three courses of unhewn stones and a course of worked cedar all around.
6:36aHe built a curtain for the court of the house’s porch in front of the temple.
7:1King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre,

7:2a widow’s son, and he was from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a Tyrian man, a bronze craftsman, filled with skill, understanding, and knowledge for doing every work in bronze. He was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.

7:3He cast the two pillars for the house’s porch. The pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a circumference of fourteen cubits encircled it. The pillar’s thickness was four fingerbreadths, with hollow spaces; and the second pillar was the same.
7:4He made two capitals to place on top of the pillars, of cast bronze. One capital was five cubits high, and the second capital was five cubits high.
7:5He made two nets to cover the pillars’ capital: one net for one capital and one net for the second capital.
7:6There was hanging work: two rows of bronze pomegranates interwoven as a net, hanging work, row upon row. He did likewise for the second capital.
7:7He set up the pillars of the temple’s porch. He set up one pillar and called it Iachoum; he set up the second pillar and called it Boaz.
7:8On top of the pillars was lily-work corresponding to the porch, four cubits.
7:9There was a beam over both pillars, and above the sides the beam formed a capital in its thickness.
7:10He made the Sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, round all around and five cubits high; thirty-three cubits in all encircled it.
7:11Supports encircled it beneath its brim all around, ten to a cubit, holding up the Sea all around.
7:12Its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily shoot, and its thickness was a palm.
7:13Twelve cattle were beneath the Sea: three facing north, three facing the sea, three facing south, and three facing east. All their hindquarters faced the house, and the Sea was above them.
7:14He made ten bronze stands. Each stand was five cubits long, four cubits wide, and six cubits high.
7:15This was the construction of the stands: they had enclosed panels, and enclosed panels between the projecting parts.
7:16On their enclosed panels between the projecting parts were lions, cattle, and cherubim, and likewise on the projecting parts. Above and below the lions and cattle were spaces, in descending work.
7:17Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze attachments; their four parts had shoulders beneath the basins.
7:18The wheels’ arms were in the stand, and the height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
7:19The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their arms, backs, and assembled work were all cast.
7:20Each stand had four shoulders at its four corners; its shoulders were of one piece with the stand.
7:21At the top of the stand was a round part half a cubit in size, all around at its top, with the beginnings of its arms and its enclosed panels; it opened onto the beginnings of its arms.
7:22Its enclosed panels had cherubim, lions, and palm trees standing, each adjoining the next toward its front, inside and all around.
7:23According to this pattern he made all ten stands, with one arrangement and one measure for all.
7:24He made ten bronze basin vessels; each basin vessel held forty choes by measure. There was one basin vessel on each of the ten stands.
7:25He placed the ten stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left. The Sea was on the right side of the house, eastward toward the southern slope.
7:26Hiram made the cauldrons, braziers, and bowls. Hiram finished all the works that he did for King Solomon in the Lord’s house:
7:27two pillars, the two twisted ornaments of the pillars on top of the pillars, and the two nets covering both twisted ornaments of the carvings on the pillars;
7:28four hundred pomegranates for both nets, two rows of pomegranates for each net, covering both twisted ornaments on both pillars;
7:29the ten stands and the ten basin vessels on the stands;
7:30the one Sea and the twelve cattle beneath the Sea;

7:31the cauldrons, braziers, bowls, and all the utensils that Hiram made for King Solomon for the Lord’s house, and the forty-eight pillars of the king’s house and the Lord’s house. All the king’s works that Hiram made were entirely of bronze.
7:32There was no measured weight of the bronze from which he made all these works, because of its great abundance; there was no limit to the weight of the bronze.
7:33In the region around the Jordan the king cast them in the thick earth, between Succoth and Sira.
7:34King Solomon placed the utensils he had made in the Lord’s house: the gold altar and the gold table on which were the loaves of the offering;
7:35the lampstands of refined gold, five on the right and five on the left before the inner sanctuary; and the lamp holders, lamps, and ladles of gold;
7:36the entranceways, nails, bowls, dishes, and censers of refined gold; and the doorframes of the innermost house, the Holy of Holies, and the gold doors of the temple house.

7:37All the work that Solomon did for the Lord’s house was completed. Solomon brought in the things his father David had consecrated and all Solomon’s consecrated things, the silver, gold, and utensils, and placed them in the treasuries of the Lord’s house.
7:38Solomon built his own house in thirteen years.
7:39He built the house with timber from Lebanon’s forest: a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with three rows of cedar pillars and cedar supports for the pillars.
7:40He paneled the house above, over the sides of the pillars. The number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen to a row.
7:41There were three beams, and space above space in three tiers.
7:42All the doorways and spaces were square and fitted with beams, with doorway facing door in three tiers.
7:43The porch of the pillars was fifty cubits long and thirty wide, joined together, with a porch in front of them, and pillars and a thick structure in front of it for the porches.
7:44There was the porch of the thrones, where he would judge, the porch of the judgment hall.
7:45He had a house where he would live, with one court opening around these, according to this workmanship; and a house for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Solomon had married, corresponding to this porch.
7:46All these were of costly stones, carved at intervals inside, from the foundation to the cornices, and outside as far as the great court,
7:47which was founded on costly, great stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits,
7:48and above, costly stones according to the measure of unhewn stones, and cedars.
7:49Around the great court were three courses of unhewn stones and a course of carved cedar.
7:50Solomon completed his entire house.

continuations: He spoke of dwelling in gloom: ‘Build My house, a splendid house for yourself, to dwell in newness.’ Is this not written in the Book of Song?”
chapters.heading: 1 Kings 8

verses.text: 8:1When Solomon had finished building the Lord’s house and his own house after twenty years, King Solomon assembled all Israel’s elders in Zion to bring up the ark of the Lord’s covenant from the City of David, which is Zion,
8:2in the month of Athanin.
8:3The priests carried the ark
8:4and the tent of testimony and all the holy utensils in the tent of testimony,
8:5while the king and all Israel were before the ark, sacrificing innumerable sheep and cattle.
8:6The priests brought the ark to its place, into the house’s inner sanctuary, the Holy of Holies, beneath the cherubim’s wings.
8:7For the cherubim had their wings spread over the ark’s place; the cherubim covered the ark and its holy things from above.
8:8The consecrated things projected, and the ends of the consecrated things could be seen from the holy places in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen outside.

8:9There was nothing in the ark except two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant, which Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the sons of Israel as they came out of the land of Egypt.
8:10When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house.
8:11The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the Lord’s glory filled the house.
8:14The king turned his face, and the king blessed all Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
8:15He said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, this day, who spoke with His mouth concerning my father David and fulfilled it with His hands, saying,

8:16‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city in any tribe of Israel in which to build a house for My name to be there; but I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there, and I chose David to be over My people Israel.’
8:17It came into the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
8:18But the Lord said to my father David, ‘Because it came into your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that it came into your heart.
8:19Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; your son who comes from your sides shall build the house for My name.’

8:20The Lord has established the word He spoke. I have risen in place of my father David and sat on Israel’s throne, as the Lord promised, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
8:21There I made a place for the ark, in which is the Lord’s covenant that the Lord made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
8:22Solomon stood before the Lord’s altar in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel and spread his hands toward heaven.
8:23He said, “Lord, the God of Israel, there is no God like Thee in heaven above or on earth beneath, keeping covenant and mercy with Thy servant who walks before Thee with all his heart,
8:24which Thou keptest for Thy servant David my father; Thou spakest with Thy mouth and didst fulfill it with Thy hands, as it is this day.

8:25Now, Lord, the God of Israel, keep for Thy servant David my father what Thou didst promise him: ‘A man of yours shall not be removed from before Me sitting on Israel’s throne, if only your children guard their ways, walking before Me as you have walked before Me.’
8:26Now, Lord, the God of Israel, let Thy word to David my father indeed be confirmed.
8:27But will God truly dwell with people on earth? If heaven and the heaven of heaven are not sufficient for Thee, how much less this house that I have built for Thy name!
8:28Look upon my supplication, Lord, the God of Israel, to hear the rejoicing that Thy servant offers in prayer before Thee, to Thee, this day,

8:29so that Thine eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which Thou saidst, ‘My name shall be there,’ to hear the prayer Thy servant prays toward this place day and night.
8:30Hear the supplication of Thy servant and Thy people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear in Thy dwelling place, in heaven; act and be merciful.
8:31“Whatever each person’s sin against his neighbor, if he takes an oath-curse upon himself to swear it, and comes and makes his declaration before Thine altar in this house,
8:32then hear from heaven, act, and judge Thy people Israel: condemn the lawless by bringing his way upon his own head, and vindicate the righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.
8:33“When Thy people Israel stumble before enemies because they have sinned against Thee, and they return, acknowledge Thy name, and pray and plead in this house,
8:34then hear from heaven, be merciful concerning the sins of Thy people Israel, and bring them back to the land Thou gavest their fathers.
8:35“When heaven is shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against Thee, and they pray toward this place, acknowledge Thy name, and turn from their sins when Thou humblest them,

8:36then hear from heaven and be merciful concerning the sins of Thy servant and Thy people Israel, for Thou wilt show them the good way in which to walk. Give rain on the land, which Thou gavest Thy people as an inheritance.
8:37“If there is famine, if there is death, if there is scorching, locust, or mildew; if their enemy afflicts them in one of their cities; whatever calamity or pain there is,
8:38whatever prayer or supplication is made by any person, each knowing the affliction of his own heart and spreading his hands toward this house,

8:39then hear from heaven, from Thy prepared dwelling place; be merciful, act, and give to each person according to his ways, as Thou knowest his heart, for Thou alone knowest the hearts of all the sons of humankind,
8:40so that they may fear Thee all the days they live on the land Thou gavest our fathers.
8:41“Also concerning the foreigner who is not of Thy people,
8:42when they come and pray toward this place,

8:43hear from heaven, from Thy prepared dwelling place, and do all that the foreigner calls upon Thee for, so that all the peoples may know Thy name and fear Thee as Thy people Israel do, and may know that Thy name is called over this house I have built.
8:44“When Thy people go out to war against their enemies by the way Thou turnest them, and pray in the Lord’s name toward the city Thou didst choose and the house I built for Thy name,
8:45then hear their supplication and prayer from heaven and uphold their cause.

8:46“When they sin against Thee—for there is no person who will not sin—and Thou bringest trouble upon them and givest them over before enemies, and their captors carry them away to a land far and near,
8:47and they turn their hearts in the land where they were deported, return, and plead with Thee in the land of their exile, saying, ‘We have sinned, acted lawlessly, and done wrong,’

8:48and they return to Thee with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their enemies, where Thou didst deport them, and pray to Thee toward their land, which Thou gavest their fathers, the city Thou didst choose, and the house I have built for Thy name,
8:49then hear from heaven, from Thy prepared dwelling place,

8:50and be merciful concerning their wrongs by which they sinned against Thee, and all their acts of faithlessness by which they were faithless to Thee. Grant them compassion before those who took them captive, so that their captors may have compassion on them,
8:51for they are Thy people and Thine inheritance, whom Thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace.
8:52May Thine eyes and ears be open to Thy servant’s supplication and the supplication of Thy people Israel, to hear them in everything for which they call upon Thee,

8:53for Thou didst set them apart for Thyself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as Thou spakest through Thy servant Moses when Thou broughtest our fathers out of the land of Egypt, Lord, Lord.”
8:53aThen Solomon spoke concerning the house when he had finished building it: “The Lord made the sun known in heaven;
8:54When Solomon finished praying all this prayer and supplication to the Lord, he rose from before the Lord’s altar, having knelt on his knees with his hands spread toward heaven.
8:55He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
8:56“Blessed be the Lord this day, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all He promised. Not one word has failed among all His good words which He spoke through His servant Moses.
8:57May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our fathers. May He not abandon us or turn us away,
8:58so that He may incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways and keep all His commandments and ordinances which He commanded our fathers.

8:59May these words, with which I have pleaded before the Lord our God, remain near the Lord our God day and night, to uphold Thy servant’s cause and Thy people Israel’s cause, each day’s matter in its day,
8:60so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord God, He is God, and there is no other.
8:61Let our hearts be complete toward the Lord our God, walking devoutly in His ordinances and keeping His commandments, as it is this day.”
8:62The king and all the sons of Israel offered a sacrifice before the Lord.

8:63King Solomon offered the peace offerings that he sacrificed to the Lord: twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the Lord’s house.

8:64That day the king consecrated the middle of the court in front of the Lord’s house, for there he offered the whole burnt offering, sacrifices, and fat of the peace offerings; the bronze altar before the Lord was too small to bear the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices of peace offerings.

8:65That day Solomon kept the feast, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the River of Egypt, before the Lord our God in the house he had built, eating, drinking, and rejoicing before the Lord our God for seven days.
8:66On the eighth day he dismissed the people and blessed them. They went, each to his tent, joyful and glad of heart for the good that the Lord had done for His servant David and His people Israel.
9:1When Solomon had finished building the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and every undertaking Solomon wished to carry out,
9:2the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as He had appeared at Gibeon.

9:3The Lord said to him, “I have heard the voice of your prayer and supplication which you made before Me. I have done for you according to your whole prayer. I have consecrated this house you did build, to put My name there for ever; My eyes shall be there and My heart always.
9:4As for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, with holiness of heart and uprightness, doing all I commanded him, and keep My ordinances and commandments,
9:5then I will establish your royal throne over Israel for ever, as I told your father David, saying, ‘A man ruling in Israel shall not be removed from you.’
9:6But if you and your children indeed turn away from Me and do not keep My commandments and ordinances which Moses set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

9:7then I will remove Israel from the land I gave them and cast away from My presence this house I consecrated for My name. Israel shall become a disappearance and a subject of talk among all the peoples.
9:8As for this lofty house, everyone passing through it will be astonished and hiss, saying, ‘Why has the Lord done this to this land and this house?’

9:9They will say, ‘Because they abandoned the Lord their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, took hold of foreign gods, bowed down to them, and served them; therefore the Lord brought this calamity upon them.’”
9:9aThen Solomon brought Pharaoh’s daughter up from the City of David to his house, which he had built for himself in those days.
9:10During the twenty years in which Solomon built the two houses, the Lord’s house and the king’s house,
9:11Hiram king of Tyre assisted Solomon with cedar timber, pine timber, gold, and everything he desired. Then the king gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
9:12Hiram came out from Tyre and went to Galilee to see the cities Solomon had given him, and they did not please him.
9:13He said, “What are these cities you have given me, my brother?” He called them Boundary, as they are called to this day.
9:14Hiram brought Solomon a hundred twenty talents of gold
9:26and a ship, concerning which King Solomon carried out work at Ezion-geber, near Elath, on the shore of the farthest sea in the land of Edom.
9:27Hiram sent in the ship men from his attendants, sailors who knew how to ply the sea, along with Solomon’s attendants.
9:28They went to Sophira, took a hundred twenty talents of gold from there, and brought it to King Solomon.
10:1The queen of Sheba heard Solomon’s name and the Lord’s name, and came to test him with riddles.
10:2She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came in to Solomon and spoke to him about everything in her heart.
10:3Solomon explained all her matters to her. No matter was overlooked by the king that he did not explain to her.
10:4When the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon’s discernment and the house he had built,

10:5Solomon’s food, the seating of his attendants, the station of his ministers, his clothing, his wine-pourers, and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the Lord’s house, she was beside herself.
10:6She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my land about your word and your discernment is true.

10:7I did not believe those speaking to me until I arrived and my eyes saw. Behold, it is not half as they reported to me! You have added good things beyond them, beyond every report I heard in my land.
10:8Blessed are your women! Blessed are these attendants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your discernment!

10:9Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you, setting you on Israel’s throne! Because the Lord loves Israel, to establish them for ever, He made you king over them to carry out judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.”
10:10She gave Solomon a hundred twenty talents of gold, very many spices, and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
10:11Hiram’s ship, which carried gold from Souphir, also brought a very great quantity of unhewn wood and precious stones.

10:12The king made the unhewn wood into supports for the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and into harps and lyres for the singers. No such unhewn wood has come upon the earth or been seen anywhere to this day.

10:13King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and asked for, besides everything he had given her through King Solomon’s hand. Then she returned and went to her land, she and all her attendants.
10:14The weight of gold coming to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
10:15besides the tribute of the subject peoples, the merchants, all the kings of the region beyond, and the satraps of the land.
10:16Solomon made three hundred spears of hammered gold; three hundred gold pieces went onto each spear.
10:17He also made three hundred shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold were in each shield. He placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
10:18The king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with tested gold.
10:19The throne had six steps, foreparts of calves behind it, and arms on each side of the seat, with two lions standing beside the arms.
10:20Twelve lions stood on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.

10:21All Solomon’s drinking vessels were gold, and the basins were gold. All the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were encased in gold. None were silver, because silver was not valued in Solomon’s days.
10:22For the king had a Tarshish ship at sea with Hiram’s ships. Once every three years a ship came to the king from Tarshish with gold, silver, and engraved and hewn stones.

10:22aThis was the undertaking for the spoil which King Solomon brought up: to build the Lord’s house, the king’s house, Jerusalem’s wall, and the citadel, to enclose the enclosure of the City of David; also Assour, Magdan, Gezer, Upper Beth-horon, Iethermath, all the chariot cities, all the horsemen’s cities, and Solomon’s undertaking which he undertook to build in Jerusalem and throughout the land, so that there might not rule over him

10:22bany of the people remaining from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites, who were not of the sons of Israel—their children remaining after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had been unable to destroy. Solomon subjected them to tribute, as it remains to this day.
10:22cBut Solomon put none of the sons of Israel into labor, because they were his warriors and attendants, his chariot commanders and his horsemen.
10:23Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in wealth and discernment.
10:24All the kings of the earth sought Solomon’s presence to hear the discernment the Lord had put in his heart.
10:25Each brought his gifts: gold vessels, clothing, stacte, spices, horses, and mules, year after year.
10:26Solomon had four thousand mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. He placed the mares in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
10:26aHe ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the foreigners and to Egypt’s borders.
10:27The king made gold and silver in Jerusalem as common as stones, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamores in the plain.
10:28Solomon’s horses came from Egypt and from Thekoue; the king’s merchants obtained them from Thekoue in exchange.

10:29The export from Egypt came up: a chariot for a hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for fifty pieces of silver. In this way they went out by sea for all the Hittite kings and the kings of Syria.

11:1King Solomon was a lover of women. He had seven hundred princesses and three hundred concubines. He took foreign wives, as well as Pharaoh’s daughter: Moabite, Ammonite, Syrian, Edomite, Hittite, and Amorite women,

11:2from the nations about which the Lord had forbidden the sons of Israel, “You shall not go in among them, and they shall not come in among you, lest they turn your hearts after their idols.” Solomon clung to these in love.
11:4When Solomon was old, his heart was not whole with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father; the foreign wives turned his heart after their gods.

11:5–8[5] Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, Moab’s idol, and for their king, the idol of the sons of Ammon, [6] and for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians. [7] He did the same for all his foreign wives; they burned incense and offered sacrifices to their idols. [8] Solomon did evil before the Lord; he did not walk after the Lord as David his father did.
11:9The Lord became angry with Solomon because he had turned his heart away from the Lord, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
11:10and had commanded him about this matter, absolutely not to follow other gods, and to take care to do what the Lord God had commanded him.

11:11The Lord said to Solomon, “Because these things have been your conduct, and you have not kept My commandments and My ordinances which I commanded you, I will surely tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your servant.
11:12Yet I will not do these things in your days, because of David your father. I will take it from your son’s hand.
11:13But I will certainly not take the whole kingdom. I will give your son one scepter, because of David My servant and because of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen.”

11:14The Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon: Ader the Idumean, and Esrom son of Eliada, who was in Rhaemmath with Hadadezer king of Zobah, his lord. Men gathered to him, and he became leader of a band and seized Damascus. They were adversaries to Israel all Solomon’s days. Ader the Idumean was of the royal line in Idumea.
11:15When David was destroying Edom, and Joab the army commander went to bury those struck down, they killed every male in Idumea—
11:16for Joab and all Israel remained there in Idumea six months, until he had destroyed every male from Idumea—
11:17Ader escaped, with all the Idumean men from his father’s attendants accompanying him, and they entered Egypt. Ader was a little boy.
11:18Men set out from the city of Midian, came to Paran, took men with them, and came to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Ader went in to Pharaoh, and he gave him a house and assigned him bread.
11:19Ader found great favor before Pharaoh, and Pharaoh gave him as wife the sister of his own wife, the older sister of Thekemina.
11:20Thekemina’s sister bore Ader Genubath her son. Thekemina brought him up among Pharaoh’s sons, and Genubath was among Pharaoh’s sons.
11:21Ader heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers and that Joab the army commander was dead. Ader said to Pharaoh, “Send me away, so I may return to my land.”
11:22Pharaoh said to Ader, “What do you lack with me? Behold, you are seeking to go to your land.” Ader said to him, “Indeed, you must send me away.” Then Ader returned to his land.
11:25This was the harm Ader did. He became resentful in Israel and reigned in the land of Edom.
11:26Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Sarira, the son of a widow, was Solomon’s servant.
11:27This was the matter concerning how he raised his hands against King Solomon: he built the citadel and closed the enclosure of the City of David his father.
11:28The man Jeroboam was strong in ability. Solomon saw that the young man was a hard worker and appointed him over the burdens of the house of Joseph.

11:29At that time Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road and took him aside from the road. Ahijah was clothed in a new garment, and both were in the plain.
11:30Ahijah took hold of his new garment which he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
11:31He said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, because thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I am tearing the kingdom from Solomon’s hand and will give you ten scepters.
11:32But two scepters shall remain his, because of My servant David and because of Jerusalem, the city I chose from all Israel’s tribes,

11:33because he abandoned Me and made provision for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, for Chemosh and Moab’s idols, and for their king, the offense of the sons of Ammon. He did not walk in My ways to do what is right before Me as David his father did.
11:34Yet I will certainly not take the whole kingdom from his hand, because I will surely oppose him all the days of his life, because of David My servant, whom I chose.
11:35I will take the kingdom from his son’s hand and give you the ten scepters.
11:36I will give his son the two scepters, so that My servant David may have a place before Me always in Jerusalem, the city I chose for Myself to place My name there.
11:37I will take you, and you shall reign over what your soul desires; you shall be king over Israel.

11:38If you keep all I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right before Me, keeping My commandments and ordinances as David My servant did, then I will be with you and build you a faithful house as I built for David.’”
11:40Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death. He arose and escaped to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and remained in Egypt until Solomon died.
11:41The rest of Solomon’s acts, all he did, and all his discernment—behold, are these not written in the Book of Solomon’s Acts?
11:42Solomon’s reign in Jerusalem lasted forty years.

11:43Solomon slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David his father. When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard—he was still in Egypt, having fled from Solomon’s presence and remained in Egypt—he made his way and came to his city, to the land of Sarira in the hill country of Ephraim. King Solomon slept with his fathers, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
12:1King Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel were coming to Shechem to make him king.
12:3The people spoke to King Rehoboam, saying,
12:4“Your father made our collar heavy. Now lighten your father’s harsh servitude and his heavy collar, which he placed on us, and we will serve you.”
12:5He said to them, “Go away until three days have passed, and return to me.” They went away.
12:6The king instructed the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was still alive, saying, “How do you advise me, so that I may answer this people?”
12:7They said to him, “If this day you become this people’s servant, serve them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants always.”
12:8He abandoned the elders’ counsel which they had given him and consulted the young men who had been brought up with him and stood before him.
12:9He said to them, “What do you advise, and what shall I answer this people who said to me, ‘Lighten the collar your father placed on us’?”

12:10The young men who had been brought up with him and stood before him said, “Thus speak to this people who told you, ‘Your father made our collar heavy; now lighten it for us.’ Thus speak to them: ‘My little part is thicker than my father’s loins.
12:11Now my father burdened you with a heavy collar, but I will add to your collar. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
12:12All Israel came to King Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them, “Return to me on the third day.”
12:13The king answered the people harshly, and Rehoboam abandoned the elders’ counsel which they had given him.

12:14He spoke to them according to the young men’s counsel: “My father made your collar heavy, but I will add to your collar. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”
12:15The king did not listen to the people, for the turn of events came from the Lord, to establish His word which He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.

12:16All Israel saw that the king had not listened to them. The people answered the king, “What share have we in David? We have no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Run away to your tents, Israel! Now shepherd your own house, David!” Israel went to their tents.
12:18The king sent Adoniram, who supervised the tribute. All Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. King Rehoboam managed to go up and flee to Jerusalem.
12:19Israel rejected David’s house, as it remains to this day.

12:20When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned from Egypt, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over Israel. None followed David’s house except Judah’s scepter and Benjamin alone.

12:21Rehoboam entered Jerusalem and summoned Judah’s assembly and Benjamin’s scepter: a hundred twenty thousand young warriors, to fight Israel’s house and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
12:22The word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,
12:23“Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, to all Judah’s house and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:

12:24‘Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up or fight your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let each return to his own house, because this matter has come from Me.’” They listened to the Lord’s word and stopped going, according to the Lord’s word.

12:24aKing Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Rehoboam his son reigned in his place in Jerusalem. He was sixteen years old when he became king, and reigned twelve years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Naanan, daughter of Anan son of Nahash, king of the sons of Ammon. He did evil before the Lord and did not walk in the way of David his father.

12:24bThere was a man from Ephraim’s hill country, Solomon’s servant, whose name was Jeroboam. His mother’s name was Sarira, a prostitute. Solomon made him a ruler of the staff over the burdens of Joseph’s house. He built Sarira in Ephraim’s hill country for Solomon, and he had three hundred horse-drawn chariots. He built the citadel through the burdens of Ephraim’s house; he enclosed the City of David and was rising up against the kingdom.
12:24cSolomon sought to put him to death. He became afraid and fled to Shishak king of Egypt, and remained with him until Solomon died.

12:24dJeroboam heard in Egypt that Solomon was dead. He spoke in the ears of Shishak king of Egypt, saying, “Send me away, so I may go to my land.” Shishak said to him, “Ask for something, and I will give it to you.”
12:24eShishak gave Jeroboam Ano as wife, the older sister of Thekemina his wife. She was prominent among the king’s daughters, and she bore Jeroboam his son Abijah.

12:24fJeroboam said to Shishak, “Do send me away, so I may go.” Jeroboam left Egypt and came to the land of Sarira in Ephraim’s hill country. All Ephraim’s scepter gathered there, and Jeroboam built a stockade there.
12:24gHis child fell very seriously ill. Jeroboam went to inquire about the child, and said to Ano his wife, “Rise and go; inquire of God about the child, whether he will live through his illness.”

12:24hThere was a man in Shiloh named Ahijah. He was sixty years old, and the Lord’s word was with him. Jeroboam said to his wife, “Rise and take in your hand for the man of God loaves, little cakes for his children, grapes, and a jar of honey.”
12:24iThe woman rose and took in her hand loaves, two little cakes, grapes, and a jar of honey for Ahijah. The man was old, and his eyes were dim for seeing.

12:24kShe set out from Sarira and went. When she entered the city to see Ahijah the Shilonite, Ahijah said to his young attendant, “Go out now to meet Ano, Jeroboam’s wife, and say to her, ‘Come in, and do not stand there, because thus says the Lord: I will send harsh things upon you.’”

12:24lAno entered to the man of God, and Ahijah said to her, “Why have you brought me loaves, grapes, little cakes, and a jar of honey? Thus says the Lord: Behold, you will leave me, and when you enter the gate into Sarira, your young women will come out to meet you and say, ‘The child is dead.’

12:24mFor thus says the Lord: Behold, I will destroy from Jeroboam’s house every male who urinates against a wall. Dogs will eat Jeroboam’s dead in the city, and the birds of heaven will eat whoever dies in the field. They will mourn the child, saying, ‘Alas, lord!’ because a good word concerning the Lord was found in him.”
12:24nThe woman departed when she heard. When she entered Sarira, the child died, and the outcry came out to meet her.

12:24oJeroboam went to Shechem in Ephraim’s hill country and gathered Israel’s tribes there. Rehoboam son of Solomon went up there. The Lord’s word came to Shemaiah the Elamite, saying, “Take a new garment which has not entered water, tear it into twelve pieces, give it to Jeroboam, and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: Take ten pieces for yourself, to clothe yourself.’” Jeroboam took them. Shemaiah said, “Thus says the Lord concerning Israel’s ten tribes.”

12:24pThe people said to Rehoboam son of Solomon, “Your father made his collar heavy upon us and made the food of his table a heavy burden. Now, if you lighten it upon us, we will serve you.” Rehoboam said to the people, “Three more days, and I will give you an answer.”

12:24qRehoboam said, “Bring the elders in to me, and I will consult them about what answer to give the people on the third day.” Rehoboam spoke in their ears according to what the people had sent to him, and the elders of the people said, “So the people have spoken to you.”

12:24rRehoboam dismissed their counsel, and it did not please him. He sent and brought in his companions and told them the same things: “These are the things the people sent to say to me.” His companions said, “Thus speak to the people: ‘My little part is thicker than my father’s loins. My father whipped you with whips, but I will rule you with scorpions.’”
12:24sThe saying pleased Rehoboam, and he answered the people as his companions, the young men, had advised him.

12:24tAll the people spoke as one man, each to his neighbor, and all cried out, “We have no share in David, nor inheritance in Jesse’s son. To your tents, Israel, because this man is fit neither for ruler nor for leader!”

12:24uAll the people dispersed from Shechem, and each went to his tent. Rehoboam took hold of himself, departed, mounted his chariot, and entered Jerusalem. All Judah’s scepter and all Benjamin’s scepter followed him.
12:24xAt the beginning of the year, Rehoboam gathered every man of Judah and Benjamin and went up to fight Jeroboam at Shechem.

12:24yThe Lord’s word came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying, “Say to Rehoboam king of Judah, to all Judah’s house and Benjamin, and to the remainder of the people: ‘Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up or fight your brothers, the sons of Israel. Return, each to his house, because this matter has come from Me.’”
12:24zThey listened to the Lord’s word and refrained from going, according to the Lord’s word.
12:25Jeroboam built Shechem in Ephraim’s hill country and lived there. He went out from there and built Penuel.
12:26Jeroboam said in his heart, “Behold, now the kingdom will return to David’s house.
12:27If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the Lord’s house in Jerusalem, the people’s heart will return to the Lord and their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me.”
12:28The king took counsel, went, and made two golden heifers. He said to the people, “Let your going up to Jerusalem be enough. Behold, your gods, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt!”
12:29He placed one in Bethel and put the other in Dan.
12:30This matter became a sin. The people went before the one as far as Dan.
12:31He made houses on high places and appointed some of the people as priests who were not from the sons of Levi.

12:32Jeroboam held a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast in the land of Judah, and went up onto the altar he had made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers he had made. He stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places he had made.

12:33He went up onto the altar he had made, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, at the feast he had fashioned from his heart. He held a feast for the sons of Israel and went up onto the altar to offer sacrifice.
13:1Behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the Lord’s word, while Jeroboam stood at the altar to offer sacrifice.

13:2He called to the altar by the Lord’s word: “Altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. He will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you.”
13:3He gave a portent that day, saying, “This is the word the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar will split, and the fat upon it will pour out.”

13:4When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had called against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” Behold, the hand he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
13:5The altar split, and the fat poured from the altar, according to the portent the man of God had given by the Lord’s word.

13:6King Jeroboam said to the man of God, “Entreat the favor of the Lord your God, and let my hand be restored to me.” The man of God entreated the Lord’s favor, and he restored the king’s hand to him, so it became as it had been before.
13:7The king said to the man of God, “Come into the house with me and eat a meal, and I will give you a gift.”
13:8The man of God said to the king, “Even if you give me half your house, I will not go in with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place.
13:9For the Lord commanded me by a word: ‘Do not eat bread, drink water, or return by the road you did travel.’”
13:10He went by another road and did not return by the road on which he had come to Bethel.

13:11An old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him all the deeds the man of God had done that day in Bethel and the words he had spoken to the king; they turned their father’s attention toward it.
13:12Their father said to them, “Which road has he taken?” His sons showed him the road by which the man of God who came from Judah had gone up.
13:13He said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” They saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.
13:14He went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak. He said to him, “Are you the man of God who has come from Judah?” He answered, “I am.”
13:15He said to him, “Come with me and eat bread.”
13:16He said, “I cannot return with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place,
13:17because the Lord commanded me by a word, ‘Do not eat bread there or drink water there, nor return by the road you did travel.’”

13:18He said to him, “I too am a prophet like you. An angel has spoken to me by the Lord’s word, saying, ‘Bring him back to yourself, to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.’” He lied to him.
13:19He brought him back, and he ate bread and drank water in his house.
13:20While they were sitting at the table, the Lord’s word came to the prophet who had brought him back.
13:21He said to the man of God who had come from Judah, “Thus says the Lord: Because you did defy the Lord’s word and did not keep the commandment the Lord your God gave you,
13:22and did return, eat bread, and drink water in this place where He told you, ‘Do not eat bread or drink water,’ your body shall certainly not enter your fathers’ tomb.”
13:23After eating bread and drinking water, he saddled the donkey for him, and he returned.
13:24He went away, and a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay thrown on the road, with the donkey standing beside it and the lion standing beside the body.
13:25Behold, men passed by and saw the dead body thrown on the road, with the lion standing beside the dead body. They came and reported it in the city where the old prophet lived.
13:26The one who had brought him back from the road heard and said, “This is the man of God who defied the Lord’s word.”
13:28He went and found his body thrown on the road, with the donkey and lion standing beside the body. The lion had not eaten the man of God’s body or crushed the donkey.
13:29The prophet lifted the man of God’s body and laid it on the donkey. The prophet brought him back into the city to bury him
13:30in his own tomb; and they mourned him, “Alas, brother!”
13:31After mourning him, he said to his sons, “If I die, bury me in this tomb where the man of God is buried. Place me beside his bones, so that my bones may be preserved with his bones,
13:32because the word he spoke by the Lord’s word against the altar in Bethel and against the high houses in Samaria will surely come to pass.”

13:33After this matter, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil. He again appointed priests of high places from some of the people. Whoever wished, he consecrated, and that person became a priest for the high places.
13:34This matter became a sin for Jeroboam’s house, bringing destruction and disappearance from the face of the earth.

14:21Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned over Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord chose from all Israel’s tribes to place His name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
14:22Rehoboam did evil before the Lord and provoked Him to jealousy with all his fathers had done and with their sins which they committed,
14:23and they built for themselves high places, standing stones, and groves on every high hill and under every shady tree.
14:24There was also a conspiracy in the land. They practiced things from all the abominations of the nations the Lord had removed before the sons of Israel.
14:25In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem.

14:26He took all the treasures of the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and the golden spears David had taken from the hands of the servants of Hadadezer king of Zobah and brought to Jerusalem. He took everything—the golden shields.
14:27King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place. The leaders of the runners who guarded the gateway of the king’s house placed them on him.
14:28Whenever the king entered the Lord’s house, the runners took the shields up and deposited them in the runners’ chamber.
14:29The rest of Rehoboam’s acts and all he did—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
14:30There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
14:31Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Abiou his son reigned in his place.
15:1In the eighteenth year of Jeroboam son of Nebat’s reign, Abiou son of Rehoboam became king over Judah.
15:2He reigned six years. His mother’s name was Maacah daughter of Absalom.
