15:3He walked in his father’s sins which he had committed before him. His heart was not whole with the Lord his God, like the heart of David his father.
15:4For David’s sake the Lord gave him a remnant, establishing his children after him and preserving Jerusalem,
15:5because David did what was right before the Lord and did not turn aside from anything He commanded him all the days of his life.
15:7The rest of Abiou’s acts and all he did—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah? There was war between Abiou and Jeroboam.
15:8Abiou slept with his fathers in Jeroboam’s twenty-fourth year and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Asa his son reigned in his place.
15:9In the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah.
15:10He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Ana daughter of Absalom.
15:11Asa did what was right before the Lord, like David his father.
15:12He removed the initiatory rites from the land and expelled all the practices his fathers had carried out.
15:13He also removed Ana his mother from being a leader, because she had held a gathering in her grove. Asa cut down her hiding places and burned them with fire at the Kidron wadi.
15:14He did not remove the high places; nevertheless Asa’s heart was whole with the Lord all his days.
15:15He brought in his father’s pillars, and he brought his own pillars into the Lord’s house—silver and gold pillars, and vessels.
15:16There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel continually.
15:17Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, so there would be no one going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

15:18Asa took the silver and gold found in the treasuries of the king’s house and gave them into his attendants’ hands. King Asa sent them to the son of Ader, son of Tabrimmon, son of Azin, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,

15:19“Make a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you gifts of silver and gold. Come, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so he will withdraw from me.”
15:20The son of Ader listened to King Asa and sent his commanders of forces against Israel’s cities. He struck Ain, Dan, Abelmaa, and all Chezrath, as far as all the land of Naphtali.
15:21When Baasha heard, he stopped building Ramah and returned to Tirzah.

15:22King Asa issued orders to all Judah as far as Ainakim. They carried away Ramah’s stones and timber with which Baasha had built. With them King Asa built the whole hill of Benjamin and the watchtower.
15:23The rest of Asa’s acts and all the power he exercised—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah? Yet in his old age he suffered in his feet.
15:24Asa slept and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
15:25Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
15:26He did evil before the Lord and walked in his father’s way and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
15:27Baasha son of Ahijah, over the house of Belaan, besieged him and struck him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the foreigners, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
15:28Baasha put him to death in the third year of Asa son of Abiou, king of Judah, and reigned.

15:29When he became king, he struck down Jeroboam’s house. He left Jeroboam no breath, until he had destroyed him, according to the Lord’s word which He spoke through His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
15:30concerning Jeroboam’s sins, how he caused Israel to sin, and his provocation by which he provoked the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger.
15:31The rest of Nadab’s acts and all he did—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
15:33In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over Israel in Tirzah, reigning twenty-four years.
15:34He did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, as he caused Israel to sin.
16:1The Lord’s word came through Jehu son of Hanani to Baasha:

16:2“Because I raised you from the ground and made you leader over My people Israel, but you did walk in Jeroboam’s way and did cause My people Israel to sin, provoking Me with their worthless things,
16:3behold, I am rousing up against Baasha and against his house. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
16:4Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will devour; anyone belonging to him who dies in the plain, the birds of the heavens will devour.”
16:5The rest of Baasha’s acts, all he did, and his mighty deeds—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
16:6Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah. Elah his son reigned in his place in the twentieth year of King Asa.

16:7Through Jehu son of Hanani, the Lord spoke against Baasha and against his house concerning all the evil he had done before the Lord, provoking Him with the works of his hands and becoming like Jeroboam’s house, and because he struck it down.
16:8Elah son of Baasha reigned over Israel two years in Tirzah.
16:9Zimri, commander of half the cavalry, conspired against him. He was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Osa, the steward in Tirzah.
16:10Zimri came in, struck him, put him to death, and reigned in his place.
16:11When he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he struck down all Baasha’s house,
16:12according to the word which the Lord spoke against Baasha’s house to Jehu the prophet,
16:13concerning all the sins of Baasha and Elah his son, how he caused Israel to sin, provoking the Lord, the God of Israel, with their worthless things.
16:14The rest of Elah’s acts and all he did—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
16:15Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. Israel’s camp was against Gibbethon, which belonged to the foreigners.
16:16The people in the camp heard it said, “Zimri has conspired and struck the king!” They made Omri, the army commander, king in Israel, over Israel, that day in the camp.
16:17Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
16:18When Zimri saw that his city had been taken, he went into a cave of the king’s house. He burned the king’s house over himself with fire and died,
16:19because of the sins he committed, doing evil before the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, as he caused Israel to sin.
16:20The rest of Zimri’s acts and the conspiracies he formed—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
16:21Then the people of Israel divided. Half the people followed Thamni son of Gonath to make him king, and half the people followed Omri.
16:22The people following Omri overpowered the people following Thamni son of Gonath. Thamni and Joram his brother died at that time, and Omri became king after Thamni.
16:23In the thirty-first year of King Asa, Omri became king over Israel, reigning twelve years. He reigned six years in Tirzah.

16:24Omri acquired the hill of Semeron from Shemer, the hill’s owner, for two talents of silver and built on the hill. He named the hill he built on Saemeron, after the name of Shemer, the hill’s owner.
16:25Omri did evil before the Lord and acted more wickedly than all who had been before him.
16:26He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the Lord, the God of Israel, with their worthless things.
16:27The rest of Omri’s acts, all he did, and his might—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
16:28Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. Ahab his son reigned in his place.

16:28aIn Omri’s eleventh year, Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king, thirty-five years old at his accession, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Gazouba daughter of Selei.

16:28bHe walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right before the Lord. But they did not remove the high places; they sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
16:28cThe agreements Jehoshaphat made, all the might he displayed, and those against whom he fought—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
16:28dHe removed from the land the remaining unions which they had undertaken in the days of Asa his father.
16:28eThere was no king in Syria—nasib.
16:28fKing Jehoshaphat made a ship for Tarshish to go to Sophir for gold. It did not go, because the ship was wrecked at Ezion-geber.
16:28gThen the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will send your attendants and my young men in the ship.” But Jehoshaphat was unwilling.
16:28hJehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Joram his son reigned in his place.
16:29In Jehoshaphat’s second year, Ahab son of Omri became king. He reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
16:30Ahab did evil before the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
16:31It was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat: he took as wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
16:32He set up an altar for Baal in the house of his offenses which he had built in Samaria,
16:33and Ahab made a grove. Ahab went on committing provocations, to provoke his soul to destruction; he did evil more than all the kings of Israel who had been before him.

16:34In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his younger son he set up its gates, according to the Lord’s word which He spoke through Joshua son of Nun.

17:1Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except through the utterance of my word.”
17:2The Lord’s word came to Elijah:
17:3“Go from here eastward and hide yourself at the Chorrath wadi, which faces the Jordan.
17:4You will drink water from the wadi, and I will command the ravens to sustain you there.”
17:5Elijah acted according to the Lord’s word and stayed at the Chorrath wadi facing the Jordan.
17:6The ravens brought him bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the wadi.
17:7After some days the wadi dried up, because there had been no rain on the land.
17:8The Lord’s word came to Elijah:
17:9“Rise and go to Zarephath in Sidonian territory. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to sustain you.”

17:10He rose and went to Zarephath, to the city gateway. Behold, a widow was there gathering wood. Elijah called after her and said to her, “Please bring me a little water in a vessel, so I may drink.”
17:11As she went to fetch it, Elijah called after her and said, “Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”

17:12The woman said, “As the Lord your God lives, I have no hearth cake, only a handful of flour in the water jar and a little oil in the flask. Behold, I am gathering two little sticks; I will go in and prepare it for myself and my children. We will eat and die.”
17:13Elijah said to her, “Take courage. Go in and do as you have said. But first make me a little hearth cake from it and bring it out to me. Afterward prepare some for yourself and your children.
17:14For thus says the Lord: ‘The water jar of flour will not be exhausted, and the flask of oil will not diminish, until the day the Lord gives rain on the land.’”
17:15The woman went and acted. She and he and her children ate.
17:16The water jar of flour was not exhausted, and the flask of oil did not diminish, according to the Lord’s word which He spoke through Elijah.
17:17After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill. His illness was very severe, until no breath remained in him.
17:18She said to Elijah, “What have I to do with you, man of God? You have come to me to bring my wrongdoings to remembrance and to put my son to death!”
17:19Elijah said to the woman, “Give me your son.” He took him from her bosom, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
17:20Elijah cried out and said, “Alas, Lord, Witness of the widow with whom I am staying—Thou hast brought harm by putting her son to death!”
17:21He breathed into the child three times, called upon the Lord, and said, “Lord my God, I pray Thee, let this child’s soul return into him!”
17:22It happened so, and the child cried out.
17:23He brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, “Behold, your son lives!”
17:24The woman said to Elijah, “Behold, I know that you are a man of God, and the Lord’s word in your mouth is true.”
18:1After many days, the Lord’s word came to Elijah in the third year, saying, “Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain on the face of the land.”
18:2Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria.
18:3Ahab called Obadiah the steward. Obadiah feared the Lord greatly.
18:4When Jezebel was striking the Lord’s prophets, Obadiah took a hundred men who were prophets, hid them fifty to a cave, and sustained them with bread and water.

18:5Ahab said to Obadiah, “Come, let us pass through the land to water springs and wadis. Perhaps we will find grass and preserve horses and mules, so they are not destroyed from among the livestock.”
18:6They divided the route between them to pass through it. Ahab went one way alone, and Obadiah went another way alone.
18:7Obadiah was on the way alone, and Elijah came to meet him alone. Obadiah hurried, fell on his face, and said, “Is it you yourself, my lord Elijah?”
18:8Elijah said to him, “It is I. Go, tell your lord, ‘Behold, Elijah is here.’”
18:9Obadiah said, “How have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into Ahab’s hand to put me to death?

18:10As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to search for you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he burned the kingdom and its territories, because he had not found you.
18:11Now you say, ‘Go, report to your lord, “Behold, Elijah is here.”’
18:12If I leave you, the Lord’s Spirit will carry you to a land I do not know. I will come to report to Ahab, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has feared the Lord from his youth.
18:13Have you, my lord, not been told what I did when Jezebel was killing the Lord’s prophets—how I hid a hundred men from the Lord’s prophets, fifty to a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
18:14Now you say to me, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Behold, Elijah is here.”’ He will kill me!”
18:15Elijah said, “As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him this day.”
18:16Obadiah went to meet Ahab and reported to him. Ahab ran out and went to meet Elijah.
18:17When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to Elijah, “Is it you yourself, the one perverting Israel?”
18:18Elijah said, “I am not perverting Israel, but you and your father’s house are, by abandoning the Lord your God; you have followed the Baalim.
18:19Now send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred fifty prophets of shame and the four hundred prophets of the groves who eat at Jezebel’s table.”
18:20Ahab sent throughout all Israel and gathered all the prophets at Mount Carmel.
18:21Elijah came near them all and said to them, “How long will you limp on both your knees? If the Lord is God, follow Him; if Baal is, follow him.” The people did not answer a word.
18:22Elijah said to the people, “I remain as the Lord’s prophet utterly alone, but Baal’s prophets are four hundred fifty men, and the grove’s prophets are four hundred.

18:23Let them give us two oxen. Let them choose one for themselves, cut it in pieces, and place it on the wood, but put no fire under it. I will prepare the other ox, but I will certainly put no fire under it.
18:24Cry out in the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord my God. The God who answers by fire—He is God.” All the people answered, “The proposal you have spoken is good.”
18:25Elijah said to the prophets of shame, “Choose one young bull for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are many. Call on the name of your god, but put no fire under it.”

18:26They took the young bull and prepared it. They called on Baal’s name from morning until noon, saying, “Hear us, Baal, hear us!” But there was no voice and no hearing. They ran about on the altar they had made.

18:27At noon Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, “Call with a loud voice, for he is a god! He has chattering to do; perhaps he is also conducting business, or perhaps he is asleep and will get up!”
18:28They called with a loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with knives and lances, until blood poured over them.

18:29They prophesied until the late afternoon had passed. When it was time for the sacrifice to go up and there was no voice, Elijah the Tishbite spoke to the prophets of offenses: “Move away now, and I will prepare my burnt offering.” They moved away and departed.
18:30Elijah said to the people, “Come near me.” All the people came near him.
18:31Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of Israel’s tribes, as the Lord had spoken to him, saying, “Israel will be your name.”
18:32He built the stones in the Lord’s name and repaired the altar that had been demolished. He made a trench around the altar, holding two metretes of seed.
18:33He piled the split wood on the altar he had made, cut the burnt offering in pieces, placed it on the split wood, and piled it on the altar.

18:34He said, “Bring me four water jars of water and pour it on the burnt offering and the split wood.” They did so. He said, “Do it a second time,” and they did it a second time. He said, “Do it a third time,” and they did it a third time.
18:35The water ran around the altar, and they filled the trench with water.

18:36Elijah cried out to heaven and said, “Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, hear me, Lord! Hear me this day with fire, and let all this people know that Thou art the Lord, the God of Israel, and I am Thy servant, and that I have done these works because of Thee.
18:37Hear me, Lord! Hear me with fire, and let this people know that Thou art the Lord God, and that Thou hast turned this people’s heart backward.”
18:38Fire from the Lord fell from heaven and consumed the burnt offering, the split wood, and the water in the trench; the fire licked up the stones and the dust.
18:39All the people fell on their faces and said, “Truly the Lord is God! He is God!”
18:40Elijah said to the people, “Seize Baal’s prophets! Let none of them be spared.” They seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Kishon wadi and slaughtered them there.
18:41Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the rain’s footsteps.”
18:42Ahab went up to eat and drink. Elijah went up onto Carmel, bent down to the ground, and put his face between his knees.

18:43He said to his young attendant, “Go up and look toward the sea.” The young attendant looked and said, “There is nothing.” Elijah said, “Go back seven times.” The young attendant went back seven times.
18:44At the seventh time, behold, a little cloud like a man’s footprint was bringing up water. He said, “Go up, tell Ahab, ‘Harness your chariot and go down, so the rain does not overtake you.’”
18:45Meanwhile the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain. Ahab wept and went to Jezreel.
18:46The Lord’s hand was upon Elijah. He bound up his waist and ran before Ahab as far as Jezreel.
19:1Ahab reported to Jezebel his wife all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed the prophets with the sword.
19:2Jezebel sent to Elijah and said, “If you are Elijah, I am Jezebel! May the god do thus to me and add more, for at this time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them!”
19:3Elijah was afraid, rose, and went for his life. He came to Beer-sheba in Judah and left his young attendant there.

19:4He himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, came, and sat under a single broom bush. He asked that his life might end and said, “Let it be enough now! I pray Thee, take my life from me, Lord, for I am no better than my fathers.”
19:5He lay down and slept there under a plant. Behold, someone touched him and said to him, “Rise and eat.”
19:6Elijah looked, and there at his head were a hearth cake of spelt and a flask of water. He rose, ate, and drank, then lay down again.
19:7The Lord’s angel returned a second time, touched him, and said to him, “Rise, eat, for the journey is too much for you.”
19:8He rose, ate, and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Mount Horeb.
19:9He entered the cave there and lodged there. Behold, the Lord’s word came to him, and He said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

19:10Elijah said, “I have been most zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the children of Israel have abandoned Thee. They have demolished Thine altars and killed Thy prophets with the sword. I remain utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.”

19:11He said, “You shall go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain. Behold, the Lord will pass by.” A great, strong wind was breaking mountains apart and crushing rocks before the Lord, but the Lord was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
19:12After the earthquake came a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. After the fire came the sound of a gentle breeze, and there was the Lord.
19:13When Elijah heard, he covered his face with his sheepskin cloak, went out, and stood beneath the cave. Behold, a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

19:14Elijah said, “I have been most zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the children of Israel have forsaken Thy covenant. They have pulled down Thine altars and killed Thy prophets with the sword. I remain utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.”
19:15The Lord said to him, “Go, return on your way, and you will come to the wilderness road of Damascus. Anoint Hazael as king of Syria.
19:16Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel-meholah, as prophet in your place.
19:17Whoever is spared from Hazael’s sword, Jehu will put to death; whoever is spared from Jehu’s sword, Elisha will put to death.
19:18You will leave seven thousand men in Israel: every knee that has not bent the knee to Baal, and every mouth that has not bowed down to him.”

19:19He went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat, who was plowing with oxen. Twelve pairs of oxen were before him, and he was among the twelve. He came upon him and threw his sheepskin cloak over him.
19:20Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “I will kiss my father and follow you.” Elijah said, “Return, for I have acted for you.”

19:21He turned back from following him, took the pairs of oxen, and sacrificed them. With the oxen’s equipment he boiled them, gave them to the people, and they ate. Then he rose, followed Elijah, and ministered to him.
20:1Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard beside the threshing floor of Ahab king of Samaria.

20:2Ahab said to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard, so it may be a vegetable garden for me, because it is nearer my house. I will give you another vineyard better than it; or, if it pleases you, I will give you silver in exchange for this vineyard of yours, and it will be a vegetable garden for me.”
20:3Naboth said to Ahab, “May my God forbid that I should give you my fathers’ inheritance!”
20:4Ahab’s spirit became troubled. He lay on his bed, covered his face, and ate no bread.
20:5Jezebel his wife came to him and said, “Why is your spirit troubled, and why are you not eating bread?”

20:6He said to her, “I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, saying, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver; or, if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my fathers’ inheritance.’”
20:7Jezebel his wife said to him, “Is this how you now act as king over Israel? Rise, eat bread, and be yourself again. I will give you Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard.”
20:8She wrote a letter in Ahab’s name, sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders and free men who lived with Naboth.
20:9It was written in the documents: “Observe a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
20:10Seat two men, sons of lawbreakers, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘He has “blessed” God and the king.’ Let them take him out and stone him, and let him die.”
20:11The men of his city—the elders and free men who lived in his city—did as Jezebel had sent to them, as written in the documents she had sent them.
20:12They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people,

20:13Two men, sons of lawbreakers, came and sat opposite him. They testified against him, saying, “You have ‘blessed’ God and the king.” They took him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
20:14They sent to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”
20:15When Jezebel heard, she said to Ahab, “Rise, take possession of Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard, which he did not give you for silver. Naboth is no longer alive; he is dead.”
20:16When Ahab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. After this, Ahab rose and went down to Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard to take possession of it.
20:17The Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
20:18“Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is in Naboth’s vineyard, because he has gone down there to take possession of it.

20:19Say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because you did murder and did take possession, therefore thus says the Lord: In every place where swine and dogs licked Naboth’s blood, dogs will lick your blood there, and prostitutes will bathe in your blood.’”
20:20Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” He said, “I have found you, because you have been sold in vain to do evil before the Lord, provoking Him.

20:21Thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I am bringing calamities upon you. I will burn out what remains after you and destroy from Ahab every male who urinates against a wall, both confined and abandoned in Israel.

20:22I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocations you have provoked and because you did cause Israel to sin.’”
20:23To Jezebel the Lord spoke, saying, “The dogs will devour her at Jezreel’s outer wall.”
20:24Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; anyone belonging to him who dies in the plain, the birds of the heavens will eat.
20:25Yet Ahab acted in vain, as he was sold to do evil before the Lord, as Jezebel his wife turned him aside.
20:26He acted most abominably by following the abominations, according to all that the Amorites had done, whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.

20:27Because of the word, Ahab was stricken before the Lord: he went about weeping, tore his tunic, tied sackcloth around his body, fasted, and put on sackcloth on the day he struck Naboth the Jezreelite.
20:28The Lord’s word came through His servant Elijah concerning Ahab, and the Lord said,
20:29“Have you seen how Ahab has been stricken before Me? I will not bring the harm in his days, but in his son’s days I will bring the harm.”

21:1The son of Ader gathered all his force, went up, and besieged Samaria, with thirty-two kings accompanying him and all the cavalry and chariots. They went up, besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
21:2He sent to Ahab king of Israel in the city,
21:3and said to him, “Thus says the son of Ader: ‘Your silver and gold are mine; your wives and children are mine.’”
21:4The king of Israel answered, “As you have said, lord king, I am yours, and so is everything of mine.”
21:5The messengers returned and said, “Thus says the son of Ader: ‘I sent to you, saying, “You shall give me your silver, gold, wives, and children.”

21:6For at this time tomorrow I will send my attendants to you. They will search your house and your attendants’ houses; the things desired by their eyes, whatever they lay their hands on, they will take.’”

21:7The king of Israel called all the elders and said, “Please understand and see that this man seeks harm. He has sent to me concerning my wives, my sons, and my daughters. I did not withhold my silver and gold from him.”
21:8The elders and all the people said to him, “Do not listen, and do not consent.”

21:9He said to the son of Ader’s messengers, “Tell your lord, ‘Everything you first sent to your servant about, I will do; but this thing I cannot do.’” The men departed and brought him back the answer.
21:10The son of Ader sent back to him, saying, “May the god do thus to me and add more, if Samaria’s dust will suffice for the foxes—for all the people, my foot soldiers!”
21:11The king of Israel answered, “Enough! Let the bent man not boast like the upright man.”
21:12When this message was answered to him, he and all the kings with him were drinking in tents. He said to his attendants, “Build a siegework!” They set a siegework against the city.

21:13Behold, a prophet approached the king of Israel and said, “Thus says the Lord: ‘Have you seen this whole great crowd? Behold, I am giving it into your hands this day, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”
21:14Ahab said, “Through whom?” He said, “Thus says the Lord: ‘Through the young attendants of the district rulers.’” Ahab said, “Who will engage in battle?” He said, “You.”
21:15Ahab mustered the young attendants of the district rulers, and there were two hundred thirty. After this he mustered the people, every man of valor: sixty thousand.
21:16He went out at noon, while the son of Ader was drinking himself drunk in Socchoth, he and the kings—thirty-two kings allied with him.
21:17The young attendants of the district rulers went out first. They sent out and reported to the king of Syria, “Men have come out of Samaria.”
21:18He said to them, “If these men are coming out for peace, take them alive; if for war, take them alive.
21:19And do not let the young attendants of the district rulers come out of the city.” The force behind them
21:20struck, each man the one beside him, and each repeated the blow against the one beside him. Syria fled, and Israel pursued them. The son of Ader, king of Syria, escaped on a cavalryman’s horse.
21:21The king of Israel went out, captured all the horses and chariots, and inflicted a great defeat on Syria.

21:22The prophet approached the king of Israel and said, “Strengthen yourself. Understand and consider what you must do, for at the return of the year the son of Ader, king of Syria, is coming up against you.”

21:23The attendants of the king of Syria said, “Israel’s God is a God of mountains and not a God of valleys; that is why He was stronger than we. But if we fight them on level ground, surely we will be stronger than they.
21:24Do this: dismiss the kings, each to his own place, and appoint satraps in their place.

21:25We will replace for you a force like the force you did lose, cavalry for cavalry and chariots for chariots. We will fight them on level ground and be stronger than they.” He listened to them and did so.
21:26At the return of the year, the son of Ader mustered Syria and went up to Aphek for battle against Israel.
21:27The children of Israel were mustered and came to meet them. Israel camped opposite them like two flocks of goats, while Syria filled the land.

21:28The man of God approached and said to the king of Israel, “Thus says the Lord: ‘Because Syria has said, “The Lord, Israel’s God, is a God of mountains and not a God of valleys,” I will give this great force into your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”
21:29They camped opposite one another for seven days. On the seventh day battle began, and Israel struck down a hundred thousand Syrian foot soldiers in one day.
21:30The survivors fled into the city of Aphek, and the wall fell on the twenty-seven thousand men remaining. The son of Ader fled and entered the house of the bedchamber, into the inner chamber.

21:31He said to his attendants, “I know that Israel’s kings are merciful kings. Let us put sackcloth on our waists and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will preserve our lives.”

21:32They tied sackcloth around their waists, put ropes on their heads, and said to the king of Israel, “Your servant the son of Ader says, ‘Please let me live.’” He said, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”

21:33The men took this as an omen, hurried, and picked up the word from his mouth: “Your brother, the son of Ader!” He said, “Come in and bring him.” The son of Ader came out to him, and they brought him up to him onto the chariot.

21:34He said to him, “I will restore to you the cities my father took from your father. You may establish outlets for yourself in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria.” “And I will send you away with a covenant.” He made a covenant with him and sent him away.
21:35One of the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the Lord’s word, “Please strike me.” But the man was unwilling to strike him.
21:36He said to him, “Because you have not listened to the Lord’s voice, behold, you are running away from me, and a lion will strike you.” He left him, and a lion found him and struck him.
21:37He found another man and said, “Please strike me.” The man struck him, delivering a blow and bruising him.
21:38The prophet went and stood waiting for the king of Israel on the road, binding his eyes with a bandage.

21:39As the king passed, he cried to the king, “Your servant went out to the army of the battle. Behold, a man brought a man to me and said, ‘Guard this man. If he escapes, your life will be for his life, or you must weigh out a talent of silver.’
21:40Your servant looked around here and there, and the man was gone.” The king of Israel said to him, “Behold, the ambushes too! You have committed murder beside me.”
21:41He hurried and removed the bandage from his eyes. The king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
21:42He said to him, “Thus says the Lord: ‘Because you did let a doomed man out of your hand, your life will be for his life, and your people for his people.’”
21:43The king of Israel went away, confounded and dispirited, and came to Samaria.
22:1He remained three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel.
22:2In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
22:3The king of Israel said to his attendants, “Do you know that Remmath-gilead belongs to us, yet we remain silent about taking it from the hand of the king of Syria?”
22:4The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go up with us to Remmath-gilead for battle?” Jehoshaphat said, “As I am, so are you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.”
22:5Jehoshaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire of the Lord this day.”

22:6The king of Israel gathered all the prophets, about four hundred men, and the king said to them, “Shall I go to Remmath-gilead for battle, or hold back?” They said, “Go up, and the Lord will surely give it into the king’s hands.”
22:7Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Is there no prophet of the Lord here, so we may inquire of the Lord through him?”

22:8The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom to inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not speak good things concerning me, only bad things: Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat king of Judah said, “Let the king not say so.”
22:9The king of Israel called a eunuch and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”
22:10The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat, each on his throne, armed, at Samaria’s gates. All the prophets were prophesying before them.
22:11Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself iron horns and said, “Thus says the Lord: ‘With these you will gore Syria until it is finished off.’”
22:12All the prophets were prophesying in the same way: “Go up to Remmath-gilead! The Lord will grant success and give even the king of Syria into your hands.”

22:13The messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Behold, all the prophets speak favorable things about the king with one mouth. Please let your words be like the words of one of them, and speak favorably.”
22:14Micaiah said, “As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I will speak.”

22:15He came to the king, and the king said to him, “Micaiah, shall I go up to Remmath-gilead for battle, or hold back?” He said, “Go up! The Lord will grant success and give it into the king’s hand.”
22:16The king said to him, “How many times must I put you under oath to speak truth to me in the Lord’s name?”
22:17Micaiah said, “Not so! I have seen all Israel scattered on the mountains like a flock without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These have no master. Let each return to his own house in peace.’”
22:18The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Did I not tell you that this man prophesies no good things for me, only bad things?”
22:19Micaiah said, “Not so—not I! Hear the Lord’s word—not so! I saw the Lord, the God of Israel, sitting on His throne, and all the army of heaven stood around Him, on His right and His left.
22:20The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Remmath-gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.
22:21A spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said, ‘I will deceive him.’ The Lord said to it, ‘By what means?’
22:22It said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ He said, ‘You will deceive him and indeed prevail. Go out and do so.’
22:23Now behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken calamities against you.”
22:24Zedekiah son of Chenaanah approached, struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, “What sort of spirit of the Lord was it that spoke in you?”
22:25Micaiah said, “Behold, you will see on that day, when you enter an inner chamber within an inner chamber to hide.”
22:26The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Emer the city ruler; and to Joash the king’s son
22:27say to put this man in prison and have him eat bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.”
22:28Micaiah said, “If you do return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me.”
22:29The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah with him went up to Remmath-gilead.
22:30The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “I will conceal myself and enter the battle, but you must put on my clothing.” The king of Israel concealed himself and entered the battle.
22:31The king of Syria had commanded his thirty-two chariot commanders, “Fight neither small nor great, but only the king of Israel.”
22:32When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat king of Judah, they said, “This appears to be the king of Israel!” They surrounded him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
22:33When the chariot commanders saw that this was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

22:34One man drew his bow with good aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate. He said to his charioteer, “Turn your hands and take me out of the battle, for I am wounded.”

22:35The battle turned into a rout that day. The king stood on the chariot facing Syria from morning until evening, and the blood from the wound poured into the hollow of the chariot. He died in the evening, and the blood of the rout ran into the hollow of the chariot.
22:36At sunset the army herald stood and said, “Each man to his own city and his own land,
22:37for the king is dead.” They came to Samaria and buried the king in Samaria.
22:38They washed the chariot at Samaria’s spring. Swine and dogs licked the blood, and prostitutes bathed in the blood, according to the Lord’s word which He had spoken.
22:39The rest of Ahab’s acts, all he did, the ivory house he built, and all the cities he made—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
22:40Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
22:41Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah. In the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel he became king.
22:42Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king and reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Selei.
22:43He walked in all the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the Lord’s eyes.
22:44Yet he did not remove the high places. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
22:45Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
22:46The rest of Jehoshaphat’s acts and his mighty deeds, all he did—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Judah?
22:51Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried beside his fathers in the City of David his father. Joram his son reigned in his place.
22:52Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned in Israel two years.
22:53He did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Ahab his father, the way of Jezebel his mother, and the sins of the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
22:54He served the Baalim, bowed down to them, and provoked the Lord, the God of Israel, according to all that had happened before him.
